title: Product decisions
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers product decisions such as features, quality, branding and packaging, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Product decisions
card: Product decisions are the choices a business makes about what it sells. They cover features, quality, branding and packaging.
Features are what the product does or includes. Quality is how well it is made and how well it performs, and it should suit what the target market expects.
A brand is the name, logo and image that identify a product. A strong brand builds trust, so customers may be willing to pay more for it.
Packaging protects the product and gives information. It also shapes how the product looks on the shelf and what customers think of it.
draft.remember: Product decisions shape what customers get and what they think of it. A strong brand builds trust and can support a higher price.

a.q: Why can a business with a strong brand often charge more than a rival with an unknown brand?
opts: Customers trust the brand, so they may pay more for it
Customers know the brand costs less to make
The brand makes the product's features all different
The brand means the packaging can be removed
a.why: A strong brand builds trust, and customers who trust a brand may be willing to pay more. Production cost is not what customers see, so a lower cost of making the product does not explain a higher price.
a.clue: Think about what a brand builds in the customer's mind.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange sells bread in plain paper bags. She switches to sturdy bags printed with her logo and a list of ingredients. Which product decision has she changed?
opts: Packaging, with some branding in the logo
Quality, because the bread itself is now better
Features, because the bread now does more
Price, because the bags cost more to buy
b.why: The bags are packaging, and the logo adds to branding. The bread has not changed, so quality and features are the same. A price is not a product decision in this card, and the bags do not change what the bread is.
b.clue: Has the bread changed, or only what it comes in?

a.best: Customers trust the brand, so they may pay more for it

b.best: Packaging, with some branding in the logo
